patches: REPAIR 1 (common/scanner.h, scan_pi_content): the trailing `advance_if_eq(lexer, chr)` became `skip_if_eq`. `advance_if_eq` is defined as `if (!eof && lookahead==chr) advance(); else return false`, so its `else` ABORTED a token whose value the test could not affect — the statements run past `mark_end`, so they are pure lookahead. A processing instruction WITH CONTENT therefore produced no `_pi_content` token at all, the construct could not complete, and the parser wrapped it in an ERROR node; with no XMLDecl the enclosing `prolog` was destroyed too, taking any DOCTYPE in it. Isolated to the byte by a 19-shape battery: the construct parses iff the byte after `?>` is a newline.

REPAIR 2 (xml/grammar.js, _intSubset): `repeat(choice($._markupdecl, $.conditionalSect, $._DeclSep))` over a named `_intSubsetItem`, plus a `conditionalSect` rule. Upstream could not reach a conditional section from an internal subset at ANY version measured — 0.5.0-0.6.x declare `conditionalSect` in the `dtd` grammar and inline it, but `_intSubset` referenced `$._markupdecl`, which does not include it; 0.7.0 does not declare it in the `xml` grammar at all. The failure wrapped the `doctypedecl` in an ERROR, the parser took a LATER `Name` as the DTD's name, and the analyzer published a Type symbol literally called `INCLUDE`.
grammarPin.patchAdmissibility: 8,888 corpus files / 6.69M nodes, ERROR and MISSING counted per file: 31 files repaired, 2 moved, 8,855 unchanged, corpus MISSING nodes 32 -> 10. BOTH movements are adjudicated by measurement in fixtures/xml/out/regression-adjudication.json: one is a standalone `.dtd` (root ERROR under every build, so never in the wired surface; upstream's separate `dtd` grammar parses it with 0 ERROR nodes) and the other is libxml2's own fuzzer-regression directory, kept by the project precisely because those files must not parse.

internal_silent._rule: The gate has exactly FOUR buckets — handled_verified, internal_silent, gap, and a design_decision carrying a node_type — so `internal_silent` is the UNION of 'walked through with no output' and 'walked through to read a child'. A pass-through is a member of it. Derived from the analyzer's own PASSTHROUGH_LITERALS plus the hidden rules, so it cannot drift; the FIRST version of this file listed only the former and the gate reported `Mixed` and `children` as in NO bucket, which is the gate being right and this file being behind.

_notes.MISSING: produced by every tree-sitter parser and not a construct: tree-sitter marks an ABSENT required token with `isMissing` on the TOKEN'S OWN type, so the string "MISSING" is never a node type a fixture can contain — a `handled_verified` row would read `uncovered: MISSING` forever. The lane's error walk does read `isMissing` off the whole tree (real-xml-analyzer.ts:819); every lane in the fleet records that read with this same row, so the class is named here rather than claimed. A node type that no fixture can witness is not evidence, and a bucket has to say which of the two it means.

decisions.ruling: an element that ADOPTS a named reusable definition it does not declare — XSLT 2.
decisions.resolution: an element that ADOPTS a named reusable definition it does not declare — XSLT 2.0's `xsl:use-attribute-sets` (§10.6) or `xsl:use-package` (§12.1), the only two in any W3C XML vocabulary that do this. Probe: every element in the XSLT namespace whose local name is one of those two, counted on the parse tree with namespace resolution applied. MEASURED 0 occurrences across the 2,500-file family-stratified draw (86 distinct node types, 2,787,237 nodes, 110 repositories), so the ruling is not falsified by that draw. Instrument B and not A because the string-shaped population here is real and A cannot see it: XSD writes the WORD `use` as an ordinary attribute value (`<xs:attribute use="required">`), and a grammar inventory would be silent about that while a reader reasonably expects it to have been considered. That attribute is a CONSTRAINT keyword whose three values (`required`, `optional`, `prohibited`) name no construct in the document, so it is not a use of anything — but this lane did not MEASURE its corpus frequency, and that is recorded as a declared limitation rather than asserted either way. DECLINED as neighbours: `xsl:import` (already an `imports` edge carrying a file path), `xsl:key` (declares a named key that is then used, so the KEY is the declaration and a query is a `references` edge), and `xs:include`/`xs:import` in XSD (same file-path reasoning). OVERTURN: a non-zero count of either element name in the XSLT namespace on the parse tree.
decisions.measured: probe and count are in the resolution; instruments in validation/m14/fixtures/xml/ontology-census.mts and validation/m14/fixtures/xml/overrides-probe.mts, executed against the table by validation/m14/fixtures/xml/ruled-gate.ts

decisions.resolution: XSD type DERIVATION — `<xs:extension base="T">` / `<xs:restriction base="T">` (XSD 1.0 Part 1 §3.4.2), emitted as role `xsd_type_derivation` with the base type as target. THIS TYPE IS EMITTED, so this row is reached only on a corpus where the analyzer produced 0 derivation edges, and the two outcomes mean opposite things. 0 derivation SITES on the tree: the corpus simply contains no XSD derivation — the Ruling is that the CORPUS is empty, not that XML lacks the construct, and the fix is a wider corpus. A derivation SITE present on the tree with 0 emitted edges: the gate reports FALSIFIED and is right, because the analyzer is failing to read a construct the corpus does use. That is the whole reason this entry exists: without it the gate's spec fallback attributes an `extends` verdict to WHATEVER RULED PROSE MENTIONS THE WORD, and on this lane that is `XML-ONTOLOGY-IMPLEMENTS`, whose resolution describes 'an implements/extends clause'. A 0 would then be graded RULED-SOUND on a decision written about a different type. OVERTURN: a non-zero derivation-site count on the parse tree of a corpus where this analyzer emits 0 `extends` edges.
decisions.measured: probe and count are in the resolution; instruments in validation/m14/fixtures/xml/ontology-census.mts and validation/m14/fixtures/xml/overrides-probe.mts, executed against the table by validation/m14/fixtures/xml/ruled-gate.ts

decisions.node_type: export_declaration / export_statement / export_list / module_export / export_spec / exported_item / public_declaration
decisions.ruling: a declaration that names what a document or module PUBLISHES.
decisions.resolution: a declaration that names what a document or module PUBLISHES. Instrument A, because an export in any W3C XML vocabulary would be an element in a published specification, and this grammar gives published elements their own node types: it produced 86 distinct node types over 2,787,237 nodes in the 2,500-file draw and NONE of the seven candidates above appears among them. Instrument A is UNSOUND for a construct written as ordinary syntax, and that exposure is real here, so the string-shaped population is measured and carried rather than assumed absent: 611 elements whose local name contains "export" across 3 files — 610 `<exports>` in `libxslt/doc/libxslt-api.xml`, `libxslt/doc/EXSLT/libexslt-api.xml` and `ghostty/DoxygenLayout.xml`, which are gtk-doc/Doxygen XML DESCRIBING the exported API of a C library and are documentation payload rather than an XML declaration, plus 1 `<exportedmodules>` in a Doxygen configuration file. The surface that would carry an `exports` edge already exists and is measured: every symbol a document publishes is reachable as a `contains` target, and `contains` resolves at BOTH ends on 100.0% of its 77,721 edges in the same draw. OVERTURN: any of the seven node types above at a non-zero count in the grammar inventory, or — independently, and as a search rather than a list of seven — any node type the grammar produces whose name contains `export` at a non-zero count over the corpus.
decisions.measured: probe and count are in the resolution; instruments in validation/m14/fixtures/xml/ontology-census.mts and validation/m14/fixtures/xml/overrides-probe.mts, executed against the table by validation/m14/fixtures/xml/ruled-gate.ts

decisions.ruling: a clause in which a declaration takes on the OBLIGATIONS of another type — an implements/extends clause, a superclass, an interface list.
decisions.resolution: a clause in which a declaration takes on the OBLIGATIONS of another type — an implements/extends clause, a superclass, an interface list. Instrument A: 86 distinct node types over 2,787,237 nodes in the 2,500-file draw, none of the five candidates above present. The nearest XML construct is XSD type DERIVATION (`<xs:extension base="T">` / `<xs:restriction base="T">`, XSD 1.0 Part 1 §3.4.2), and that is EMITTED as `extends` — 1,033 derivation sites over 95 files in this draw, 354 `extends` edges — because derivation names a base TYPE, which is the relation `extends` carries. What XML has no way to write is an obligation without a base: no element in any W3C XML vocabulary declares that its target satisfies another type's interface. The string-shaped population is measured and carried: 5 elements across 4 files — 2 `<interface>` in `ghostty/src/apprt/gtk/winproto/wayland/protocols/vicinae-hotkey-v1.xml`, which DECLARE a Wayland protocol interface rather than implement one, and 3 `<abstract>` in DocBook (`libxslt/doc/tutorial/libxslttutorial.xml`, `otp/lib/xmerl/doc/examples/xml/xmerl.xml`, `otp/lib/xmerl/doc/examples/xml/xmerl_xs.xml`), which are PROSE about an abstract class in a C++ manual. All five are generic `element` nodes in no vocabulary namespace, which is exactly why instrument A does not fire on them and a local-name probe would have. OVERTURN: any of the five node types above at a non-zero count, or an element in a vocabulary namespace whose defined semantics are interface satisfaction.
decisions.measured: probe and count are in the resolution; instruments in validation/m14/fixtures/xml/ontology-census.mts and validation/m14/fixtures/xml/overrides-probe.mts, executed against the table by validation/m14/fixtures/xml/ruled-gate.ts

decisions.ruling: an expression or element that CREATES an instance of a declared construct.
decisions.resolution: an expression or element that CREATES an instance of a declared construct. Instrument A: 86 distinct node types over 2,787,237 nodes in the 2,500-file draw, none of the five candidates above present, and the inventory contains no construction form of any kind — the 86 are prolog, element, attribute, content, DOCTYPE and its declarations, entity/notation declarations, conditional sections, PI, CDSect/CDATA and the anonymous punctuation tokens. Measured from the other side as well, because instrument A alone would be the json lane's mistake: 0 elements whose local name is new / instantiate / newinstance / create, across the same draw. The nearest XML constructs are an XSD `element` DECLARATION (which declares a type; it does not create a value) and an XSLT `xsl:element` / `xsl:copy-of` instruction (which create an output node from a name attribute, and the name is already a `references` edge) — in both cases the document names something rather than instantiating a declared type, which is the distinction this ruling rests on. OVERTURN: any of the five node types above at a non-zero count, or any node type the grammar produces whose name contains `new` or `instantiat` at a non-zero count over the corpus.

notApplicable.concept: RULED types, and the instrument each ruling rests on
notApplicable.measured: Four of the ten ontology types are RULED with a corpus measurement, not with prose, and each names the probe that produced its number and the count that would overturn it. `uses` (instrument B, parse-tree count): 0 occurrences of `xsl:use-attribute-sets` or `xsl:use-package` in the XSLT namespace over a 2,500-file draw. `exports` (instrument A, grammar inventory): none of 7 export-declaration node types among the 86 the wired grammar produces over 2,787,237 nodes, with 611 string-shaped `<exports>`/`<exportedmodules>` elements adjudicated as gtk-doc/Doxygen payload describing a C library's API. `implements` (A): none of 5 supertype-clause node types among the 86, with 5 string-shaped hits adjudicated as 2 Wayland `<interface>` DECLARATIONS and 3 DocBook `<abstract>` prose. `instantiates` (A): none of 5 construction node types among the 86, and 0 elements named new/instantiate/newinstance/create. Overturn conditions are in script/m14/xml-ruled.ts, whose probes are executed by validation/m14/fixtures/xml/ruled-gate.ts.

notApplicable.concept: calls / extends / overrides — NOT applicable, and this entry is the record of that being WRONG
notApplicable.measured: This entry previously claimed all four of `calls`, `extends`, `implements`, `overrides` and `instantiates` inapplicable, on the reasoning that an XSD names a type by an ATTRIBUTE VALUE so `base=` is a `references` edge. The M60 ontology census overturned it by measurement: `calls` is emitted for XSLT `xsl:call-template` (XSLT 1.0 §6, 548 edges), `extends` for XSD `<xs:extension base=>`/`<xs:restriction base=>` type derivation (XSD 1.0 §3.4.2, 438 edges), and `overrides` for XSLT 1.0 §5.5 competing template rules — that last one only after script/m14/ontology-coverage-gate.ts reported this lane's RULED verdict FALSIFIED over 11,456 files (3 sites in 3 files, e.g. libxslt/tests/docbook/fo/toc.xsl lines 180 and 190). The reasoning was not wrong about the SYNTAX: `base=` is an attribute value. It was wrong about the RELATION, because a vocabulary element that defines a relation is a declaration of that relation however its operand is spelled. Kept as a record because a reader comparing this spec against an older one needs to see that the claim changed and why.

routed (`.dtd` is in EXTENSION_LANGUAGE) but NOT representable: the xml grammar's `document` rule requires a document element, so a standalone DTD's root node type is ERROR. Measured: `cond_sect1.dtd` 11 ERROR nodes, `cond_sect2.dtd` 8, the W3C `XMLSchema.dtd` 170 — while upstream's SEPARATE `dtd` grammar parses all of them with 0. Filed as owed, with its measurement, in grammars/tree-sitter-xml/PIN.md; the corpus files are declared negative controls rather than excluded by a glob.

kindRulings.contains: structural containment read straight off the tree: element->element, element->attribute, element->namespace, DTD->declaration, declaration->content-model member, declaration->notation, PI->target. Every contains TARGET is a published symbol in the same file — enforced structurally, not by convention, and pinned by `xml/dtd-declarations` (`every contains target resolves to a symbol in the same file`).
kindRulings.references: a NAME, never a written value. The target of an XSD/RelaxNG/XSLT reference is the LOCAL NAME and the prefix rides in metadata, because a prefix in a target is a value where a name belongs (M60.R10). An edge is emitted only when the target resolves in the document or is a specification built-in — 1,319 unresolved values are REFUSED rather than published.
kindRulings.imports: a FILE PATH, which is the one case where a value IS the right target: a DOCTYPE's ExternalID, a DTD entity's or notation's ExternalID, a StyleSheetPI/XmlModelPI `href`, and an XSD `schemaLocation` URI. 630 distinct schemaLocation targets and 11 external-ID imports were emitted where the pre-fix lane emitted 0. Added 2026-10-26: an XSLT `<xsl:import href>` is also a FILE PATH and is emitted as `imports` (role xslt_stylesheet_import) - a module import with import precedence (XSLT 1.0 2.6.2), which is why it is NOT `part_of` while its sibling `<xsl:include href>` is (XSLT 1.0 2.6.1 splices content).

line.note: every relationship carries a line, and 100% of them are on the line the TARGET NAME is written on (M59.A7 / #825). Pre-fix: the external-ID edge took the ExternalID node's line, so a multi-line PUBLIC doctype pointed at the keyword — 310 wrong-line edges, now 18. Pinned by all 8 fixtures, and by the multi-line doctype in `xml/dtd-declarations`, which is the shape that makes the keyword-line mutant non-vacuous.

occurrences.note: edge collapse is COUNTED, not hidden. Edge identity is `source|type|target`, so N declarations of one pair necessarily share one edge — 492,774 occurrences on 45,297 edges. The edge keeps the EARLIEST line the name is written on, not the first the LIFO walk reached. Pinned by `xml/edge-collapse`.

syntaxErrors.note: a symbol or edge from a file the analyzer reports as erroneous says so. Pre-fix: 27,228 symbols over 177 files, unlabelled, and the shipped 'creates no recovery symbols' check was a FIXTURE ACCIDENT. Suppressing them would be wrong (177 of 177 are `##` Maven-archetype templates), so they are labelled. Pinned by `xml/recovery-labelling`, including the negative half — a clean file carries no label, so the flag cannot become noise.

declaredName.note: in a declaration vocabulary the DECLARED name is an attribute VALUE, and the tag name is kept as `meta.tagName` so the structural reading is carried rather than overwritten. Gated on the element's EFFECTIVE NAMESPACE: 29,196 `name` attributes outside any declaration vocabulary are DATA and must not be renamed, which is why the rule is not tag-gated. Recall 0.045 -> 0.696 over 26,578 in-vocabulary declarations.

resolvable.note: a `references` edge records whether its target resolves `in-document` or is a specification `builtin`, so a consumer can tell a resolved edge from a built-in one without re-deriving the namespace bindings.

coverage._rule: THE CONTRACT for this lane, in the shape script/m14/coverage-block-gate.ts asserts. `implemented` = a type the PRODUCTION path (parseFile) emits AND the corpus exercises, each with its whole-population count in `_implemented_measured`; `corpusUnexercised` = a type the analyzer emits that no file in this corpus exercises; `excluded` = a type carrying the class `grammar-absence` (which leaves the denominator) or `zero-sites` (which does not), each with a COUNT. Every type in none of those three lists is a GAP and STAYS in the denominator. There is no `unclassified` entry in this block and no `zero-sites` one. THE LINE THIS LANE DRAWS for `grammar-absence`, stated so a reader can contest it: a type is absent only when NEITHER the wired grammar's NODE TYPES NOR the corpus's ELEMENT/ATTRIBUTE NAME SPACES contain a construct whose operand names a declaration THE SAME DOCUMENT carries (or a specification builtin) — the same resolution bar this lane's own edge emission applies, where 1,319 unresolved `references` values are REFUSED rather than published. A construct that occurs with an in-document-resolving operand is NOT absent; it is a gap in this analyzer.

part_of._why: IMPLEMENTED 2026-10-25/26 AT RUNG R3 WITH NO GRAMMAR CHANGE, in the TWO vocabularies that have a textual-inclusion construct. THE CONSTRUCT: `<xi:include href>` (XInclude 1.0 4.1) and `<xsl:include href>` (XSLT 1.0 2.6.1) both REPLACE the directive with the named document's content, so the included document is a FRAGMENT of the including one - it shares the including document's single scope, contributes no module, and cannot be resolved as a separate unit once included: the part_of contract in src/ast/types.ts, and the same construct class as cpp #include "...", fsharp #load, php include/require, erlang -include and typescript /// <reference path>. R3 because each construct is a NAMESPACED ELEMENT the pinned grammar already parses as an ordinary element with an Attribute href; R1/R2 would buy nothing. DETECTION IS BY RESOLVED NAMESPACE AND ELEMENT NAME, never by the written prefix (the fixture pins an `<include>` outside every inclusion vocabulary, which emits nothing). THE TARGET IS A SYMBOL, NOT A PATH (the measured cpp result: a path target resolved 0 of 4,612 rows because the arbiter resolves target strings against SYMBOL NAMES): the target is the included document's module STEM (basename, no directory, no extension), the written href rides in metadata.partPath. `partRole` is mandatory and is "library" on every row (this document carries the directive; XML has no `part of` spelling, so XML never produces the "part" half). THE DIRECTION IS THE DIRECTIVE'S OWN: source is the file carrying the directive - the DOCUMENT ELEMENT, because XML publishes no file-level symbol. XInclude's parse="text" IS STILL part_of (decided): a text inclusion splices bytes as character data instead of element content, but another file's content still becomes part of THIS document and contributes no module; recorded as metadata.parseMode. A REMOTE href is REFUSED on the same rule imports uses. MEASURED over the WHOLE admitted population (11,593 git-tracked files <= 512 KiB with a routed extension, 202 repos, root .corpus): 50 candidate files screened, all parsed; 95 SITES in 14 files through parseFile, emitting 94 EDGES / 95 OCCURRENCES. CHANNEL SPLIT: xinclude_include 6 sites / 3 files -> 5 rows / 6 occurrences (two identical hrefs share one source|type|target key); xslt_include 89 sites / 11 files -> 89 rows / 89 occurrences. HREF CLASSES, the wall this row carries: 92 of 95 name an ADMITTED file; 2 name a file that EXISTS but is not admitted by the router's extension set (libxslt's docbook stylesheets include `../VERSION`, an extensionless file); 1 names something ABSENT (otp/lib/odbc/doc/src/specs.xml -> ../specs/specs_odbc.xml, not in this corpus); 0 remote; 0 empty. NEAR MISSES MEASURED, not claimed absent: xsl:import 43 sites / 36 files - a MODULE IMPORT with import precedence (XSLT 1.0 2.6.2) that emits `imports` (42 rows after 1 remote refusal), NEVER part_of (a fixture forbids its stem as a part_of target); RELAX NG `<include href>` = 0 sites, so the schema-merge class (which belongs to imports beside XSD xs:include) is EMPTY in this corpus, stated rather than claimed absent; the pre-REC 2003 XInclude namespace 1 site (libxslt/doc/tutorial2/libxslt_pipes.xml:655, a DocBook `<programlisting>` DISPLAYING the directive) and `<include>` in no namespace 1 site are adjudicated near misses. CROSS-CHECK: each channel's census site count equals the analyzer's own summed occurrences (xinclude 6=6, xslt_include 89=89, xslt_import 42=42 after its 1 declared refusal) - instruments validation/m14/fixtures/xml/inclusion-census.mts + .json. Fixtures xml/xinclude-part-of and xml/xsl-include-part-of pin both channels and both boundaries. The DERIVED declaration and the whole-population closure arm are still owed and are named as owed here, not claimed.

mixes_in._why: IMPLEMENTED 2026-10-26 AT RUNG R3: XSD definition composition is the one construct in this language that composes reusable definitions into a type WITHOUT declaring a supertype relation. `<xs:group ref="G"/>` inside a complexType composes G's content model into the type (XSD 1.0 3.8.2: the containing type's content model IS the referenced group's) and `<xs:attributeGroup ref="G"/>` composes G's attribute declarations (3.6.2). The composed definitions BECOME PART OF the type, and the type neither extends the group nor declares any conformance to it - the mixes_in contract in src/ast/types.ts. R3 because `ref=` is an ordinary attribute the grammar already parses. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE CARRIER, never the attribute name: only xs:group and xs:attributeGroup in the XSD namespace compose; a `ref=` on an ELEMENT is a reference (the impostor class, measured 326 substitutionGroup sites + element refs and pinned by the fixture's forbid rows). DIRECTION: source = the class composing the mixin = the NEAREST NAMED DECLARATION above the carrier (the carrier xs:group is a vocabulary tag no document declares - the same 438/438 fabricated-source defect extends measured), target = the composed group's LOCAL name. Collected then decided after the walk, because a group may be declared after the type that composes it. REFUSED when the name resolves nowhere (M60.R10). MEASURED over the WHOLE admitted population (11,593 git-tracked files <= 512 KiB, 202 repos, root .corpus): 518 construct SITES measured by the discriminator census (296 group ref / 55 files: 256 in-file, 17 cross-file, 23 absent; 222 attributeGroup ref / 60 files: 109 in-file, 110 cross-file, 3 absent) -> through parseFile 415 EDGES / 420 OCCURRENCES / 52 FILES, resolvability split 360 in-document + 55 external (the cross-file half: a composition whose target this document's own xs:include/xs:import brings in). The 518-vs-420 difference is the refusal class plus edge collapse, and both halves are stated rather than netted. NEAR MISSES MEASURED, not claimed absent: substitutionGroup 326 sites / 37 files - XSD's IS-A for elements, whose TYPE-level relation is derivation and stays `extends` (the impostor class the Lead's instruction names); xs:redefine 1 site (a merge channel); use-attribute-sets 38 sites / 9 files (XSLT 1.0 7.1.4 attribute-set composition - the same mixin shape in the XSLT vocabulary, DECLINED this turn and named as the open candidate because its lane ruling XML-ONTOLOGY-USES already measures it); RELAX NG combine 12 sites / 1 file (definition MERGE, not composition into a type). Fixture xml/xsd-definition-composition fires both carriers and FORBIDS the element-ref impostor, the type= use, the base= derivation (one construct one label) and the XSD built-in. xml fixtures 35/0 -> 36/0.

XML therefore EXPRESSES a use and this corpus exercises it with BOTH ends in-document, while src/ast/real-xml-analyzer.ts contains 0 `RelationshipType.Uses` sites — the analyzer emits nothing. A node-type-only probe cannot see an attribute key, the same blind spot that gave HCL a wrong ruling for docker-bake's `inherits = [...]`. Because it is a gap and not a grammar-absence it STAYS in the denominator: applicable 7, not 6. Raw: validation/m14/fixtures/xml/use-construct-census.json

ATTRIBUTE SPELLINGS: android:onClick / android:onLongClick / generic onclick / onClick / on-click / listener / callback = 0 sites, 0 files across the entire population (there is no Android XML in this corpus: 0 AndroidManifest.xml files exist). `handler=` = 4 sites in 1 file (pixie amqp0-9-1.stripped.xml), and its values name AMQP PROTOCOL CLASS NAMES (`handler="connection"`, `handler="channel"`) that this XML describes for a C++ code generator - not callables, and no XML document in the corpus declares them. xsl:element's `element=` = 0 sites in the `element="{...}"` AVT callable spelling; the plain form names an output ELEMENT QName (an AVT), not a procedure. excluded.label: renders
excluded.from: THE COMPONENT-MODEL TEST, measured over the WHOLE 11,593-file admitted population by validation/m14/fixtures/xml/extended-types-census.mts (695 candidates parsed). XML has no component model: nothing in any W3C XML vocabulary is a COMPONENT that renders another COMPONENT, and XSLT templates are a separate language's construct executed by an XSLT processor, not a render tree. EVERY CANDIDATE WAS COUNTED AND EACH IS A DIFFERENT RELATION: svg:use 11,307 sites / 156 files - a FRAGMENT reference (`xlink:href="#id"`, measured split: 7,246 `#fragment` spellings across the corpus, 0 external-file hrefs on use), and its target is an element `id` the analyzer correctly does not model as a declaration, so the reference pass refuses it (verified by probe: `use --contains--> href` and nothing else) - a use CLONES a graphic node, it does not render a component, and the fragment target is `references`' refusal class, not a component identity; xsl:call-template 1,528 sites / 104 files - ALREADY `calls` (402 edges in the coverage census, XSLT 1.0 §6), and a template is a procedure, not a component; xsl:apply-templates 4,167 sites / 258 files - template DISPATCH by match pattern, names no component at all; xsl:value-of 1,841 sites / 329 files - an XPath VALUE read. THE NEAREST MISS, carried rather than buried: an SVG `<use>` that referenced a SYMBOL/GROUP DEFINITION would be the closest thing to rendering a component in this corpus, and its 7,246 sites name FRAGMENT ids - a same-document reference the analyzer's own `references` rule refuses because an `id` is not a declared name, which is a RESOLVABILITY statement about id-addressing, not a component-model claim. Raw: validation/m14/fixtures/xml/extended-types-census.json (ren_svg_use 11,307/156, ren_xslt_call_template 1,528/104, ren_xslt_apply_templates 4,167/258, ren_xslt_value_of 1,841/329). OVERTURN (the falsifier, and the instrument that counts it): a vocabulary element whose defined semantics are that one COMPONENT renders another - the census's renders buckets would count it on the parse tree the moment the corpus gains such a vocabulary (a UI framework in routed XML, or an SVG `use` whose href names an external component file rather than a fragment); all four buckets carry `sitesDetail` with file:line for re-measurement.
excluded.quote: a component RENDERS another component: source = the rendering symbol, target = the rendered component.
